related_questions.question: Do I need to print an Indian e-Visa?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, you need to print your Indian e-Visa. You should print the Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) that you receive via email after your e-Visa application is approved. This printed copy should be carried with your passport when you travel to India.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, you need to print your Indian e-Visa

text_blocks.snippet: Here's why and what to do:

list.title: Official Requirement:
list.snippet: The email approving your e-Visa will explicitly state that you need to print it out.

list.title: Airport Check-in & Immigration:
list.snippet: You'll need to present the printed e-Visa, along with your passport, at the airport upon arrival in India.

list.title: Biometric Information:
list.snippet: At the airport, your biometric information (fingerprints) will be collected, and the visa sticker will be placed in your passport.

list.title: Multiple Copies:
list.snippet: It's recommended to print two copies of your e-Visa, keeping one with you and another with your travel documents.

list.title: Digital Copy:
list.snippet: While a digital copy is not mandatory, it's a good idea to have one on your phone or other device as a backup.
